title: The Double-Edged Sword of Information: Revealed versus Hidden Lotteries in School Choice
abstract: arXiv:2609.34074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In school choice, a lottery number is often used by the matching mechanism to break ties when more students prefer the same school than the number of seats available. In practice, in recent years, the NYC Public Schools started revealing the lottery number to students. Theoretical findings from prior literature suggest that revealing the lottery number strictly improves the number of matches under the deferred acceptance algorithm. However, these theoretical results are based on the over-simplifying assumption that all students share the same preference ranking for schools. In this work, we relax this assumption and allow students to have heterogeneous preference rankings. Under a game-theoretic model where student strategies form a Bayesian Nash equilibrium, we characterize scenarios where revealing the lottery number can either improve or worsen the matching outcome, measured by two metrics of the match rate and social welfar

translated_title: 信息的双刃剑：学校选择中的公开与隐藏摇号
translated_abstract: 在学校选择机制中，当偏好同一所学校的学生数量超过可用名额时，匹配机制通常会使用摇号号码来打破平局。在实践中，近年来纽约市公立学校开始向学生公开摇号号码。先前文献的理论结果表明，在延迟接受算法下，公开摇号号码能够严格提高匹配数量。然而，这些理论结果基于一个过度简化的假设，即所有学生对学校的偏好排序完全相同。在这项工作中，我们放宽了这一假设，允许学生拥有异质的偏好排序。在学生策略构成贝叶斯纳什均衡的博弈论模型下，我们以匹配率和社会福利这两个指标衡量匹配结果，刻画了公开摇号号码既可能改善也可能恶化匹配结果的各类情形。
tldr: 本文放宽了“所有学生偏好相同”的假设，在贝叶斯纳什均衡的博弈论模型下证明：学校选择中公开摇号号码是一把双刃剑，既可能提高也可能降低匹配率与社会福利。
en_tdlr: Relaxing the assumption of homogeneous student preferences, this paper shows under a Bayesian Nash equilibrium game-theoretic model that revealing lottery numbers in school choice is a double-edged sword—it can either improve or worsen match rate and social welfare.
